text.p: Following are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Caretaker Foreign Minister Sahibzada Yaqub Khan informed U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher about "some difficulties in establishing the elections in Pakistan," State Department spokesman Nick Burns stated on Friday.
- The caretaker government is preparing a list of all loan defaulters who had obtained loans since 1985 and secured relief by way of write-offs, rescheduling and restructuring.
- The Federal Investigation Agency arrested Shaukat Ali Kazmi, president of the private Allied Bank Ltd, on charges of issuing loans in violation of rules.
- The National Tariff Commission has proposed that the caretaker government cut import tariffs on raw materials to boost the flagging engineering industry, sources said.
- Foreign banks have asked the State (central) Bank of Pakistan to extend the deadline of a high-yield concessionary deposit scheme beyond December 10.
- The state-run Pakistan Telecommunication Co Ltd has devised a new strategy to cover the revenue losses it might incur due to tariff cuts by the AT&T, sources said.
- Privatisation of major state-owned companies, including Pakistan International Airlines, Pakistan State Oil and some commercial banks, is likely to start within the next two months.
- The caretaker government rejected a proposal of the National Tariff Commission for abolition of regulatory duty on imports.
- The Taleban Islamic militia of Afghanistan forced a United Nations-chartered plane to land at Shindand airport on Saturday.

- Out of nine bids received by the Trading Corporation of Pakistan for the import of 50,000 tonnes of crystal white sugar, only two parties qualified, but both quoted rates at least $30 per tonne higher than prevailing international rates.
- Tehrik-e-Insaaf chief and former cricketer Imran Khan has said Pakistan must retain its nuclear option for self-defence.
